# Control Narrative: Sanitary Lift Station LS-12

I made some engineering decisions while drafting. They are flagged here and listed again in Section 10:

1. **Lag stop is not defined.** I proposed a lag stop setpoint and a shared speed curve for both pumps.
2. **The LSL-121 float can stop all pumping if it fails.** If LSL-121 hangs or is falsely active, its hardwired stop prevents both pumps from running, and the wet well overflows. I made LSHH-121 override the LSL-121 stop in the hardwired logic.
3. **There is little margin between LSHH-121 and overflow.** If LIT-121 fails, the station runs on floats and starts pumping only at LSHH-121. The time to overflow at peak inflow must be checked.
4. **No flow meter, pump protection relays, generator signals, or overflow detection were listed.** I proposed signals and marked them as open items.
5. **Overflow is a permit event.** I added event logging with timestamps that does not depend on the radio link.

## 1. Purpose and Boundaries

LS-12 receives gravity sanitary sewer flow into the wet well. Pumps P-121 and P-122 move the flow into the force main.

| Boundary | Interface |
|---|---|
| Upstream | Gravity sewer into the wet well. This is not controlled. |
| Downstream | Force main. A check valve on each pump discharge prevents backflow. These valves are mechanical, with no signals. |
| Overflow | Overflow pipe at SP-09 to the creek. An overflow is a permit violation. |
| Power | Utility supply, automatic transfer switch ATS-120, and standby generator EG-120. |
| Supervisory | Central SCADA over licensed radio. |

**Control objective:** Keep the wet well level between SP-02 and SP-06. Prevent overflow. Record every overflow event for permit reporting.

**Out of scope:** Force main control, odor control, and SCADA master configuration.

**SIS:** No safety instrumented function is assigned to LS-12. The float backup is an independent BPCS layer, not a SIF. If a HAZOP or LOPA assigns a SIL to overflow prevention, put that function in an IEC 61511 SRS and refer to it from this document (OI-01).

## 2. Equipment and Signals

The instrument index is the master source. The signals below are what this narrative uses. Tags marked "proposed" are not yet in the index (OI-02).

| Tag | Description | Type | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| LIT-121 | Wet well level, submersible pressure transducer, range SP-01 | AI, 4-20 mA | Given |
| LSL-121 | Low level float at SP-08 | DI, plus hardwired | Given |
| LSHH-121 | High-high level float at SP-07 | DI, plus hardwired | Given |
| P-121 / P-122 | Submersible pumps, VFD driven | — | Given |
| HS-121 / HS-122 | HOA switch, Auto position | DI | Proposed |
| HS-121H / HS-122H | HOA switch, Hand position | DI | Proposed |
| YI-121 / YI-122 | VFD running feedback | DI | Proposed |
| YA-121 / YA-122 | VFD fault | DI | Proposed |
| TSH-121 / TSH-122 | Motor winding over-temperature | DI | Proposed |
| XA-121 / XA-122 | Seal leak (moisture) | DI | Proposed |
| SC-121 / SC-122 | VFD speed command | AO or network | Proposed |
| SI-121 / SI-122 | VFD speed feedback | AI or network | Proposed |
| HY-121 / HY-122 | VFD run command | DO | Proposed |
| YS-120 | Hardwired float backup relay energized | DI | Proposed |
| JS-120 | MCC power healthy (phase monitor) | DI | Proposed |
| ATS-120 | ATS in emergency position | DI | Proposed |
| EG-120 | Generator running, generator fault, generator low fuel | DI x3 | Proposed |
| UPS-120 | UPS on battery, UPS fault | DI x2 | Proposed |

Pump numbering convention: a requirement written for P-121 also applies to P-122 with matching tags.

## 3. States and Transitions (ISA-106)

The station uses state-based control. Sequence-based control is used for pump start, pump stop, and power restore (Section 5).

### 3.1 Pump States (per pump)

| State | Name | Entry Condition | Allowed Exits |
|---|---|---|---|
| PS-0 | Off | HOA in Off | PS-1, PS-2 |
| PS-1 | Hand | HOA in Hand | PS-0, PS-2 |
| PS-2 | Auto Available | HOA in Auto, no fault active or latched, not Out of Service | PS-3, PS-4, PS-5, PS-0, PS-1 |
| PS-3 | Auto Running | PS-2, PLC run command on, and YI-121 true | PS-2, PS-4, PS-0, PS-1 |
| PS-4 | Faulted | Fault in Attachment B, or fail-to-start, or fail-to-stop | PS-2 after fault clears and operator reset. PS-0 or PS-1 by HOA. |
| PS-5 | Out of Service | Operator disables the pump from SCADA | PS-2 after operator enables it |

A pump is **available** only in PS-2 or PS-3.

### 3.2 Station States

| State | Name | Entry Permissives | Allowed Exits |
|---|---|---|---|
| ST-00 | Initializing | PLC cold start, or loss of JS-120 | ST-01, ST-02, ST-03, ST-04, ST-05 through SEQ-03 only |
| ST-01 | Auto Idle | LIT-121 good, at least one pump available, no pump running in Auto | ST-02, ST-04, ST-05, ST-00 |
| ST-02 | Auto Lead | LIT-121 good, lead pump in PS-3, lag pump not running | ST-01, ST-03, ST-04, ST-05, ST-00 |
| ST-03 | Auto Lead + Lag | LIT-121 good, both pumps in PS-3 | ST-02, ST-04, ST-05, ST-00 |
| ST-04 | Float Backup | LIT-121 bad, or a float/LIT discrepancy (FR-LS12-060) | ST-01 after LIT-121 is good and the operator resets. ST-05, ST-00. |
| ST-05 | Manual | No pump available | ST-01 when at least one pump becomes available. ST-00. |

### 3.3 Station Transitions

| ID | From → To | Condition | Initiator | Automation Level |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T01 | ST-00 → ST-01/02/03/04/05 | SEQ-03 complete. The target state is set by SEQ-03 step 5. | Auto | Automatic |
| T02 | ST-01 → ST-02 | LIT-121 ≥ SP-03 | Auto | Automatic |
| T03 | ST-02 → ST-03 | LIT-121 ≥ SP-04 and a second pump is available | Auto | Automatic |
| T04 | ST-03 → ST-02 | LIT-121 ≤ SP-05, or one pump leaves PS-3 | Auto | Automatic |
| T05 | ST-02 → ST-01 | LIT-121 ≤ SP-02, or the lead pump leaves PS-3 with no replacement available | Auto | Automatic |
| T06 | Any auto state → ST-04 | LIT-121 bad for SP-22, or discrepancy per FR-LS12-060 | Auto | Automatic |
| T07 | ST-04 → ST-01 | LIT-121 good for SP-23 **and** operator pushes RESET LEVEL CONTROL | Operator | Operator-prompted |
| T08 | Any → ST-05 | No pump available | Auto | Automatic |
| T09 | ST-05 → ST-01 | At least one pump available and LIT-121 good | Auto | Automatic |
| T10 | Any → ST-00 | JS-120 false, or PLC cold start | Auto | Automatic |

The hardwired float backup (YS-120) works independently of all PLC states. See Attachment B.

## 4. Regulatory Control

### 4.1 Pump Speed versus Level

This loop is a level-to-speed schedule. It is not PID and has no tuning values.

| Item | Definition |
|---|---|
| PV | LIT-121, filtered with time constant SP-24 |
| Output | SC-121 and SC-122, in Hz |
| Action | Direct. Speed increases as level increases. |
| Function | Speed = SP-10 + (SP-11 − SP-10) × (PV − SP-03) / (SP-04 − SP-03) |
| Clamp | The output is never below SP-10 or above SP-11 |

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-LS12-001 | The PLC sends the speed from the function in 4.1 to each pump in PS-3. | FAT: Inject PV at SP-02, SP-03, the midpoint of SP-03 and SP-04, SP-04, and SP-06. Read SC-121 at each point. Check it against the calculated value within SP-25. |
| FR-LS12-002 | When the PV is below SP-03, the speed command is SP-10. | FAT: Inject PV between SP-02 and SP-03 with the pump running. |
| FR-LS12-003 | When the PV is above SP-04, the speed command is SP-11. | FAT: Inject PV above SP-04. |
| FR-LS12-004 | In ST-03, both pumps receive the same speed command from 4.1 (proposed, OI-04). | FAT: Run both pumps. Ramp PV down from SP-06 to SP-05. Check that SC-121 equals SC-122. |
| FR-LS12-005 | VFD acceleration and deceleration ramps are VFD parameters. They are set per the VFD parameter list (OI-11). | SAT: Parameter check. |

### 4.2 Mode Behavior

| HOA | PLC Control | Speed Source | Interlocks Active |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hand | None. PLC monitors only. | VFD preset SP-12 | Hardwired items per Attachment B |
| Off | None | — | — |
| Auto | Full PLC control | SC-121 from 4.1, or SP-13 when YS-120 is energized | All items in Attachment B |

There is no cascade or override control.

## 5. Sequences

### 5.1 Lead/Lag and Alternation Rules

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-LS12-010 | The PLC designates one available pump as lead and the other as lag. | FAT: Check that the designation is shown on the HMI. |
| FR-LS12-011 | At each completed lead stop (SEQ-02), the lead designation moves to the other pump if that pump is available. | FAT: Run three level cycles. Check that the lead alternates P-121, P-122, P-121. |
| FR-LS12-012 | If only one pump is available, that pump is lead for every cycle. | FAT: Put P-122 in Off. Run two cycles. |
| FR-LS12-013 | The PLC keeps the lead designation, run hours, and start counts through a PLC power cycle. | FAT: Cycle PLC power. Check that values are retained. |
| FR-LS12-014 | The operator can force the lead pump from SCADA. The force is for the next cycle only. | FAT: Force P-122 as lead. Check one cycle, then normal alternation. |
| FR-LS12-015 | The PLC blocks a start when a pump exceeds SP-15 starts per hour or is within SP-16 minimum off time. In that case, the PLC uses the other available pump. | FAT: Simulate the start count at SP-15. Check that the other pump starts. |
| FR-LS12-016 | When the PV is at or above SP-06, the PLC ignores the start limits in FR-LS12-015 (proposed, OI-05). | FAT: Block both pumps by start count. Raise PV to SP-06. Check that a pump starts. |

### 5.2 SEQ-01: Pump Start (applies to lead and lag)

**Trigger:** Lead start when PV ≥ SP-03. Lag start when PV ≥ SP-04.

| Step | Action | Transition Condition | Timeout | Failure Response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Check that the pump is in PS-2 and is not start-blocked (FR-LS12-015/016). | Permissive true | None. Evaluated once. | Select the other available pump and restart SEQ-01. If none is available, raise the "No pump available" alarm. Stay in the current state. |
| 2 | Set the speed command per 4.1. Energize HY-121. | YI-121 true | SP-14 | De-energize HY-121. Set the pump to PS-4 (fail-to-start). Raise the alarm. Run SEQ-04. |
| 3 | Monitor SI-121 against SC-121. | SI-121 within SP-26 of SC-121 | SP-27 | Raise the "Speed deviation" alarm. Keep the pump running. |
| 4 | Count the start. Set the pump to PS-3. | — | — | — |

### 5.3 SEQ-02: Pump Stop

**Trigger:** Lag stop when PV ≤ SP-05 in ST-03. Lead stop when PV ≤ SP-02 in ST-02.

| Step | Action | Transition Condition | Timeout | Failure Response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | De-energize HY-121. Set SC-121 to SP-10. | YI-121 false | SP-17 | Set the pump to PS-4 (fail-to-stop). Raise a high-priority alarm. Keep HY-121 de-energized. The hardwired LSL-121 stop is the backup. |
| 2 | Lead stop only: apply FR-LS12-011. | Immediate | — | If the other pump is not available, keep the current lead. |
| 3 | Start the SP-16 off timer for the stopped pump. | — | — | — |

### 5.4 SEQ-03: Power Loss and Restart

**Trigger:** JS-120 false, or PLC cold start.

| Step | Action | Transition Condition | Timeout | Failure Response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | De-energize all run commands. Log the power-loss event with a timestamp. Enter ST-00. | JS-120 true continuously for SP-18 | SP-19 | Raise the "Station power not restored" alarm. Continue to wait. |
| 2 | Wait for the SP-20 restart delay. | Timer complete | — | — |
| 3 | If PV ≥ SP-02 and LIT-121 is good, run SEQ-01 for the lead pump. | Lead in PS-3, or no start needed | SEQ-01 timeouts | Per SEQ-01 |
| 4 | Wait for the SP-21 stagger delay. If PV ≥ SP-04, run SEQ-01 for the lag pump. | Lag in PS-3, or no start needed | SEQ-01 timeouts | Per SEQ-01 |
| 5 | Select the station state from Section 3.2 entry permissives. | State entered | — | — |

Step 3 uses SP-02, not SP-03. This lets the station recover a wet well that was filling during the outage.

### 5.5 SEQ-04: Pump Failure Transfer

**Trigger:** A running pump leaves PS-3 for any reason other than a SEQ-02 stop.

| Step | Action | Transition Condition | Timeout | Failure Response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | If the failed pump was lead, designate the other available pump as lead. | Immediate | — | If no pump is available, enter ST-05. |
| 2 | If PV ≥ SP-02, run SEQ-01 for the new lead. | New lead in PS-3 | SEQ-01 timeouts | Per SEQ-01 |
| 3 | If the failed pump was lag, take no replacement action. | — | — | The alarm from the fault remains active. |

### 5.6 Requirements Traced to Sequences

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-LS12-020 | The PLC starts the lead pump per SEQ-01 when the PV rises to SP-03. | FAT: Ramp PV up. Check that HY-121 energizes at SP-03 ± SP-25. |
| FR-LS12-021 | The PLC starts the lag pump per SEQ-01 when the PV rises to SP-04. | FAT: Ramp PV. |
| FR-LS12-022 | The PLC stops the lag pump per SEQ-02 when the PV falls to SP-05. | FAT: Ramp PV down. |
| FR-LS12-023 | The PLC stops the lead pump per SEQ-02 when the PV falls to SP-02. | FAT: Ramp PV down. |
| FR-LS12-024 | Fail-to-start acts per SEQ-01 step 2. | FAT: Hold YI-121 false. Check alarm at SP-14, PS-4, and P-122 start. |
| FR-LS12-025 | Fail-to-stop acts per SEQ-02 step 1. | FAT: Hold YI-121 true after the stop. |
| FR-LS12-026 | Power restart acts per SEQ-03. | FAT: Drop JS-120 with PV above SP-04. Restore it. Check timing of SP-18, SP-20, and SP-21. SAT: Repeat on generator. |
| FR-LS12-027 | Pump failure transfer acts per SEQ-04. | FAT: Set YA-121 with P-121 running as lead. |
| FR-LS12-028 | A PS-4 fault stays latched until the fault clears and the operator pushes RESET. | FAT: Clear the fault. Check that the pump stays in PS-4 until RESET. |

## 6. Interlocks and Permissives

All interlocks are in **Attachment B, Cause-and-Effect Chart LS-12-CE-001**. This narrative does not restate that logic.

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-LS12-030 | The PLC and hardwired circuits do each effect in Attachment B for each cause. | FAT: Execute each C&E cell. Hardwired cells are tested on the panel with simulated floats. |
| FR-LS12-031 | Hardwired float backup items work with the PLC powered down. | FAT: Remove PLC power. Operate LSHH-121 and LSL-121 simulators. Check pump run and stop. |
| FR-LS12-032 | The PLC reads YS-120. It logs each energization with a timestamp. | FAT: Operate LSHH-121. Check the event log. |

## 7. Alarms

Alarm priorities, setpoints, and responses are in the rationalized ISA-18.2 alarm database for LS-12 (OI-06). Attachment C lists the alarm conditions this narrative creates, as input to rationalization.

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-LS12-040 | The PLC creates each alarm in the LS-12 alarm database as configured there. | FAT: Trigger each alarm against the database. |
| FR-LS12-041 | When the PV is at or above SP-09, the PLC logs the overflow start time. When the PV falls below SP-09 minus SP-28, the PLC logs the end time and the duration. | FAT: Ramp PV through SP-09. Check the log entries. |
| FR-LS12-042 | The PLC keeps overflow and power events in a local buffer of at least SP-29 events. It sends them to SCADA when communications return. | FAT: Disconnect the radio. Create an overflow event. Reconnect. Check that SCADA receives the event with the original timestamp. |
| FR-LS12-043 | The PLC clock synchronizes to the SCADA time source (OI-12). | FAT: Offset the PLC clock. Check that it resynchronizes. |

## 8. Abnormal Handling

| ID | Condition | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| FR-LS12-050 | LIT-121 bad PV (signal outside SP-30, or a channel fault) | After SP-22, enter ST-04. Stop all PLC level-based pump commands. The hardwired float backup controls the pumps. Raise an alarm. | FAT: Open the LIT loop. Check ST-04, the alarm, and no PLC starts. Operate LSHH-121 and check the hardwired start. |
| FR-LS12-051 | LIT-121 restored | Stay in ST-04 until LIT-121 is good for SP-23 and the operator pushes RESET LEVEL CONTROL (T07). | FAT: Restore the loop. Check that the station waits for RESET. |
| FR-LS12-060 | Float/LIT discrepancy | If LSHH-121 is active and the PV is below SP-07 minus SP-31 for SP-32, enter ST-04 and raise an alarm. If LSL-121 is active and the PV is above SP-02 plus SP-31 for SP-32, raise an alarm only. | FAT: Simulate each combination. |
| FR-LS12-061 | Communications loss to SCADA | Detect loss after SP-33 without a heartbeat. Continue local control with the last valid setpoints. Keep any Out of Service and lead-force settings. SCADA shows all LS-12 data as stale. | FAT: Disconnect the radio. Check that the station keeps cycling and the stale flags appear at SCADA. |
| FR-LS12-062 | Remote setpoint validation | Reject a SCADA setpoint write that breaks the order in Attachment A, note 1. Keep the old value. Send a rejection status. | FAT: Write lead stop above lead start. Check the rejection. |
| FR-LS12-063 | Utility power loss | ATS-120 and EG-120 transfer power without the PLC. The PLC monitors ATS-120, EG-120, and UPS-120. The PLC runs SEQ-03 on JS-120 loss and on return, including retransfer to utility. | FAT: Simulate the inputs. SAT: Do a live utility-fail test. |
| FR-LS12-064 | PLC and radio power | The PLC, radio, and LIT-121 loop are on UPS-120 for at least SP-34. | SAT: Open the UPS input. Time the runtime. |
| FR-LS12-065 | PLC failure | All PLC run outputs are energize-to-run. When the PLC fails, all Auto pumps stop and the hardwired float backup controls them. SCADA detects the failure as a communications loss. | FAT: Halt the PLC. Check that outputs de-energize and the hardwired backup works. |
| FR-LS12-066 | Fail positions | On loss of power, VFDs and pumps stop. There are no valves under automatic control. Check valves are mechanical. | FAT: Check by inspection of the drawings. |

| Power | JS-120, ATS-120, EG-120, UPS-120 | — | — |
| Events | Overflow log and power log | Export | — |

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-LS12-070 | The HMI shows each item in the table above. | FAT: Walk through the HMI with Operations. |

## Attachment B: Cause-and-Effect Chart LS-12-CE-001 (draft)

Key: **S** = stop. **R** = run. **A** = alarm. **(H)** = hardwired, works without the PLC. **(P)** = PLC.

| Cause | P-121 | P-122 | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| LSHH-121 active | R (H) at SP-13, if HOA in Auto | R (H) at SP-13, if HOA in Auto | Sets the YS-120 latch. A (P). |
| LSL-121 active | S (H), all HOA positions (OI-15) | S (H), all HOA positions | Resets the YS-120 latch. **Blocked while LSHH-121 is active** (OI-10). |
| TSH-121 active | S (H) | — | Pump goes to PS-4. A (P). |
